problem: Farmers lack field level data to decide on irrigation, frost and pests; Instacrops provides IoT sensors plus satellite and drone analytics.
business_model: Subscription for sensors and analytics dashboard

founders.name: Mario Bustamante
previous_startups: IoT device startup sold to a major LATAM retailer (first exit, per YC page)
founders.background_notes: Built IoT devices that sold over 11,000 units; idea came from an agronomist partner describing frost losses, per press.

competitors.name: Agrosmart
competitors.what: Brazilian soil and climate sensors with agronomic recommendations
competitors.traction_then: Reaches farmers in Latin America (current figure 100,000, date of the figure not clear)

technical_complexity.rationale: Field hardware, connectivity in rural areas and data analytics together; standard IoT engineering but operationally hard across countries.

defensibility.rationale: Installed sensors and farm history data create some lock-in, but sensors and satellite analytics are widely available.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows incumbents absorbing it; an agtech press report says it first moved from hardware toward software as hardware commoditized.

market_need_then: LAVCA (Apr 2021) says Instacrops sells sensor based monitoring for weather, pests and irrigation; the company reported 12% average yield gains and 300+ farms at its YC application.

branding.brand_signature: The Internet of Plants tagline used in Chilean press

rebrands.why: Not stated; site title now reads Instacrops.AI Smart Agricultural Solutions

brand_strength.rationale: Descriptive and friendly, similar to other Insta names; the Internet of Plants phrase appears in Chilean press, but no evidence of community or iconic status.

pivots.why: Press says hardware became commoditized; the date is not stated.

outcome_analysis: Instacrops is active and expanded across Chile, Colombia and Mexico, raising about 2.8M in 2021 and an extension with SQM in late 2022. It moved from frost sensors toward software and now AI agents. The company reports over 200K monthly revenue at its YC application, which is self reported. Funding stayed modest and no later large round was found.
notes: Stages are other because the opened LAVCA piece does not state Series A; Blueberries Consulting calls the 2021 round Series A and Caplight calls the Dec 2022 extension Series A, while Seedtable calls it pre-Series A with total round US$5.5M. The 2022 amount is null because only a total is reported. Totals vary by database (PitchBook $5.95M, Caplight $9.13M). Company homepage fetch returned only a title. Headquarters is Santiago per YC but one source says San Francisco. Competitor sources are undated.
